chips.title: Enforce the five-finding cap when a review is recorded
chips.summary: Recording a review keeps the five most severe findings as actionable and marks the rest deferred, in a fixed order, and the run records how many review dispatches it used.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.1, the first of Phase 4. It builds on the ported cycle and the Lugos shims, both finished before this board existed, so no prerequisite steps are listed.
Both board files passed the Dias parsers before work began; now writing the failing test for a seven-finding result.
198 tests pass, 16 of them new. A seven-finding review run through the command line recorded five actionable and two deferred, in severity order.
Done. The cap applies to structured findings; a prose reviewer answer is recorded unchanged, so the byte-parity baseline with the Lugos scripts still holds.

chips.title: Keep the recorded findings when a repeat record is refused
chips.summary: A second attempt to record findings for the same review is refused before anything is written, so the first recorded set and its result file stay as they were.

evidence.message: A defect found while landing the finding cap: a refused repeat record replaced the saved findings. Not a plan slice; it protects what the cap writes.

chips.title: Check an image review against the installed policy before sending
chips.summary: Before a review with screenshots is sent, it is checked against the installed Autowork image policy. A refusal stops with a message; nothing is sent or cut down to text.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.2. It extends the send step that the finding-cap step taught to count dispatches; a refused check must not count as one.

chips.title: Turn a tap on a page into the element it landed on
chips.summary: Given a point on a page, the helper reports the innermost element there as a selector with its data attributes, in a form a finding can carry.

evidence.message: Plan slice S4.5. It builds on the browser evidence helpers from the style-guide phase, which finished before this board existed, so no prerequisite steps are listed.
